paths.description: Supplied entry URL and intended primary corporate-banking entry journey. It represents the only browser-visible template because the response contains no links or controls.
Raw/crawler representation comparison to test indexing and no-JavaScript visibility.
Route discovery via DOM links, /robots.txt, and /sitemap.xml. No additional archetype was discoverable.

findings.summary: The public entrypoint does not communicate the banking service or a next action.
findings.evidence: The target root responds 404 and renders only “Not Found”; it does not identify ICICI Corporate Internet Banking or offer a next action.
findings.suggestedFix: Restore the intended entry route. If this URL is obsolete, redirect it to the supported corporate banking sign-in or a branded route-selection page.

findings.summary: The primary banking journey cannot start because the root is an HTTP 404 with no controls.
findings.evidence: The intended banking entry journey cannot begin: the root document is HTTP 404 and contains zero links, controls, and forms.
findings.suggestedFix: Serve the supported sign-in/registration journey at this entrypoint or issue a permanent redirect to it, then test the full path end to end.

findings.summary: The 404 state gives users no way to recover.
findings.evidence: The error message has no home link, retry, support route, incident reference for browser users, or other recovery control.
findings.suggestedFix: Replace the generic server error with a branded error state that offers safe links to home/sign-in, retry, and support, preserving context without exposing sensitive detail.

findings.summary: The error surface ignores the user’s dark color preference.
findings.evidence: Dark-mode screenshot is pixel-equivalent in presentation to the light screenshot: white canvas and black text, with no color-scheme declaration or authored CSS.
findings.suggestedFix: Declare color-scheme: light dark and use system colors or light-dark() for the error-page surface and text.

findings.summary: The mobile response uses a desktop-sized 980 CSS-pixel layout viewport.
findings.evidence: At a requested 360x800 mobile viewport, layout reports hasViewportMeta=false and an effective 980 CSS-pixel layout viewport, so the page is desktop-scaled instead of adapting.
findings.suggestedFix: Add <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1"> and verify the restored page reflows at narrow widths without preventing zoom.

findings.summary: Missing viewport configuration undermines expected mobile reflow and zoom behavior.
findings.evidence: No viewport meta is present; Chrome uses a 980 CSS-pixel mobile layout viewport at a 360-pixel device viewport, preventing normal mobile reflow.
findings.suggestedFix: Add the standard width=device-width viewport declaration without maximum-scale or user-scalable restrictions, then test at 320–400 CSS pixels and browser zoom.

findings.summary: The error page has generic title metadata and no description.
findings.evidence: Title is generic “404 Not Found” and meta[name=description] is absent.
findings.suggestedFix: Give the branded recovery page a specific title and concise meta description; ensure real service pages each have unique metadata.

findings.summary: There is no crawlable onward route, viewport meta, or robots resource.
findings.evidence: The document has no anchors, no viewport meta, and /robots.txt returns 404, leaving no crawlable route or mobile-friendly signal.
findings.suggestedFix: Expose real href links to supported public routes, add viewport metadata, and serve an intentional robots.txt policy.

findings.summary: Normal clients receive 404 while the crawler user agent receives a different HTTP 200 error document.
findings.evidence: HAR and curl record HTTP 404 for normal/browser clients; canonical, robots meta, sitemap, and hreflang are absent, and /sitemap.xml also returns 404.
findings.suggestedFix: Restore or redirect the canonical entry URL, serve consistent status/content across user agents, publish canonical/indexing signals on public pages, and add a sitemap where appropriate.

findings.summary: The response lacks CSP and nosniff despite otherwise using HTTPS, HSTS, and SAMEORIGIN framing protection.
findings.evidence: Direct response is HTTPS with HSTS and X-Frame-Options, but no Content-Security-Policy or X-Content-Type-Options is present.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a restrictive Content-Security-Policy suitable for the banking app and X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff; retain and verify HSTS and clickjacking protection.

findings.summary: Several browser-enforced policy headers are absent.
findings.evidence: Direct response has HSTS and X-Frame-Options: SAMEORIGIN, but lacks CSP/frame-ancestors, Referrer-Policy, Permissions-Policy, and X-Content-Type-Options.
findings.suggestedFix: Define least-privilege Referrer-Policy and Permissions-Policy, express clickjacking protection in CSP frame-ancestors, and adopt Trusted Types/origin isolation where the restored app’s threat model warrants them.

findings.summary: The server failure state is a dead end rather than an intentional recovery experience.
findings.evidence: The HTTP 404 state is a generic server page with no useful recovery option; Lighthouse also aborts with ERRORED_DOCUMENT_REQUEST.
findings.suggestedFix: Handle unknown routes and upstream failures with a stable branded page, correct status, safe retry/support actions, and no infinite loading or misleading success.

findings.summary: The document omits language and direction metadata.
findings.evidence: DOM probe reports html.lang and html.dir as empty, so assistive technology and language-sensitive rendering cannot identify the content language or direction.
findings.suggestedFix: Set an accurate html lang value and dir where needed; use logical CSS properties when rebuilding the branded response.

findings.summary: A sensitive banking flow is wholly unavailable at the supplied entry URL.
findings.evidence: A corporate banking entry URL exposes no authentication or account flow at all because the root returns 404; users cannot verify, enter, cancel, or recover the sensitive journey.
findings.suggestedFix: Restore the supported account entry journey, make its destination and security context unambiguous, and verify cancellation, support, reauthentication, autocomplete, and passkey behavior on the real flow.

findings.summary: The bare error page provides no navigational cue or onward focus target.
findings.evidence: The error state contains no link, focus target, navigation cue, or directional transition to guide the user toward a safe next step.
findings.suggestedFix: Add clear, real href links to the supported sign-in, home, and support destinations, with visual hierarchy that makes the safest next step obvious.

Build an intentional branded and recoverable HTTP error experience
